docs.purpose: The place an operator creates and manages the businesses that pay to advertise in the product — a builder or designer who buys a sponsored slot. It lists every advertiser account with a detail view for each one, and it is where an account is set up, edited, and deactivated. Nothing like it exists today because the product has never had a paying advertiser.
docs.data_story: Nothing is built yet, so nothing is measured here. As specified it would read `advertisers` — of which `advertisers` does **not exist yet** and must be declared, migrated and drift-asserted before this page can render a single row.
docs.under_126: **NEW.** It does not exist; it is generated from descriptors from its first commit, through the LIST renderer (a collection with declared pagination, recycling and empty/offline states). It is **100% generated** — which is the point: if the descriptor set is incomplete or an archetype profile is wrong, this page is visibly empty or visibly wrong on commit 1, and cannot be faked by hand.

checks.why: R-12 / Spec 128 §3 rule B6: every admin mutation writes exactly one admin_audit_log row and an audit failure fails the request. It is blocking because 9 of the 15 mutating admin routes measured today write no row at all, and the pre-batch rule says an unaudited mutation blocks conversion of the surface that calls it.
Rule 14: advertisers does not exist yet, so every declared column, type, nullability, index and Class-D policy is asserted against the live catalog both directions before the page writes a row.

R-18: this surface is admin, but the same advertisers table is also read by the advertiser principal through Class D — a mutation contract that drifted to authenticated would hand an advertiser its own edit button.
The product has never had a paying advertiser, so empty is the expected first state and must read as "none yet", not as a failed load.
A failed write must render inline beside the field, never as a silent no-op — Spec 128 rule 12, an unhandled state is a FAIL.
The LIST profile requires it; a desktop admin page keeps no cached projection, so the answer is descriptive.
The detail half is a single-parameter key by advertiser_id, per the DETAIL hygiene rule.
contact_user_id points at a person; the projection must be an explicit pick-by-name whitelist that set-equals the contract, never a row spread.

invariants.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM advertisers a WHERE a.contact_user_id IS NOT NULL AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM profiles p WHERE p.id = a.contact_user_id)
invariants.why: An advertiser whose contact points at no profile cannot be reached, and the account would look managed while being unreachable.

invariants.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM admin_audit_log WHERE action LIKE 'advertiser.%' AND admin_uid IS NULL
invariants.why: R-12 as data: an audit row with no acting admin is an unattributable mutation, which is the compliance hole admin-audit.ts's own header names.

plausibility.sql: SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE active), count(*) FROM advertisers
plausibility.why: Zero active advertisers with a non-zero total is either a correct business state or a deactivation bug, and the two are indistinguishable from a single count — the same plausible-zero trap the estate has already paid for.

limitations.what: The admin_audit_log row this surface writes cannot be named in emits.ledger_events[].
limitations.measured: surface.schema.json's emits.ledger_events[] is closed to property_view · pdf_send · offer_impression · offer_click · export · parcel_id_translated — all usage_events events. admin_audit_log is a second append-only ledger (Spec 126 §2.2.1 P10 names all three by name) with no token, so emits.answer is "ledger" and the audit row is carried in breadcrumbs[] plus a ledger_row_present check.

limitations.what: The LIST required-field profile in Spec 126 §3.1 mandates list.item_archetype, list.pagination and list.recycling — and, for the DETAIL half, sections[], and surface.schema.json has no property for any of them (the top level and every category are additionalProperties:false).
limitations.measured: Every allOf block in scripts/surfaces/_schema/surface.schema.json is `"then": true` — the archetype profiles are declared in prose in Spec 126 §3.1 and enforced by nothing, so these fields can neither be declared here nor caught missing.

limitations.what: The row is emitted as LIST although Spec 126 §2.2 assigns it "LIST + DETAIL".
limitations.measured: identity.archetype is a single closed value in surface.schema.json; there is no composite. LIST is the nearest single value and the DETAIL half is declared through query_key (single-parameter by advertiser_id) and the detail states, not by a second row.

notes: Report §1.1 row 13 gives the archetype as 'LIST + DETAIL'; emitted here as LIST (the enum's nearest single value) with the DETAIL half recorded in this note. VERIFIED AGAINST THE TREE: no CREATE TABLE for advertisers, offers or ad_slots exists anywhere in migrations/ — the report's claim holds. DESIGNED, NOT MEASURED. This is one of the two rows that MUTATE, so R-12/B6 binds: emits.answer is "ledger" and the audit row is blocking. But admin_audit_log has NO token in the closed emits.ledger_events[] vocabulary (property_view · pdf_send · offer_impression · offer_click · export · parcel_id_translated are all usage_events events), so the row is carried in breadcrumbs[] plus a ledger_row_present check and the gap is filed in limitations.
